statement.p: Find \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r for \vec F = 4 y\vec i - (\sin y)\vec j on the curve counterclockwise around the unit circle C starting at the point (1,0).

static.solution: C is parameterized by \vec r=\cos t\,\vec i+\sin t\,\vec j,\qquad\mbox{for } 0\le t\le 2\pi, so \vec F(t) = 4\sin t\,\vec i - \sin{(\sin t)}\,\vec j \quad \text{and} \quad \vec r\,'(t)=-\sin t\,\vec i + \cos t\,\vec j. Thus, \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{2\pi} (4\sin t\,\vec i - \sin{(\sin t)}\,\vec j)\cdot (-\sin t\,\vec i+\,\cos t\,\vec j) dt =\int_0^{2\pi}(-4\sin^2 t - \sin{(\sin t)}\cos t) dt Using an identity to rewrite the first term, we get =\int_0^{2\pi}\bigg[-2(1-\cos 2t) - \sin{(\sin t)}\cos t\bigg] dt Integrating, using a substitution to integrate the last term in the integrand, we obtain: =\bigg[-2(t - \frac{1}{2} \sin 2t) +\cos{(\sin t)}\bigg]\bigg|_0^{2\pi} =-4\pi \quad \text {units of work}
